explanation: Article 4 makes admission a decision of the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council, so a permanent member can hold an applicant out for as long as it likes. From 1946 both blocs did that, and membership became something to trade. Portugal was refused for nine years. It entered in December 1955 in a package of sixteen states the blocs agreed on to clear the backlog. The Charter’s design is why the admission took the form of a bargain over a list rather than a judgement on Portugal, and why Portugal found inside an Assembly majority it could not veto.
